record.title: Planar Barnette-type conjecture for sink-regular bipartite digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a sink-regular $(3,4)$-bipartite digraph that is planar, and let $Q_1,Q_2,Q_3$ be disjoint bases of $M_1(D,\1)$. A rounded $1$-factor $J$ is an object with associated set $\operatorname{dc}(J)$.

**Barnette-type conjecture.** There exists a rounded $1$-factor $J$ such that

$$
\operatorname{dc}(J)=Q_1
$$

and $D\setminus J$ is connected.

If true, this conjecture implies that every planar digraph whose dicuts have size at least three has three disjoint dijoins. Its resemblance to Barnette's conjecture for planar cubic bipartite graphs is noted in the source.
record.source_name: Ahmad Abdi, Gérard Cornuéjols and Michael Zlatin, “On packing dijoins in digraphs and weighted digraphs”, arXiv:2202.00392 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00392

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: Zeilberger–Reed conjecture on 3-connected planar linear normal lambda-terms
record.statement:
A planar linear normal $\lambda$-term is a linear normal $\lambda$-term whose syntactic diagram is planar; call it **3-connected** when its syntactic diagram is 3-connected. For $n\geq 0$, consider such terms with $n+2$ variables. **Zeilberger–Reed conjecture.** The number of 3-connected planar linear normal $\lambda$-terms with $n+2$ variables is

$$
\frac{2^n}{(n+1)(n+2)}\binom{2n+1}{n},
$$

which is also the number of bipartite planar maps with $n$ edges. This conjecture proposes a precise enumerative correspondence between highly connected planar lambda-terms and bipartite planar maps; the supplied source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Wenjie Fang, “Bijections between planar maps and planar linear normal λ-terms with connectivity condition”, arXiv:2202.03542 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.03542

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: Tightness of the function-field Sárközy bound for square differences
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $P_{q,n}$ be the set of polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of degree less than $n$, and let $A\subset P_{q,n}$ be a set containing no nonzero $k$th-power difference. Suppose that $k\geq2$, $\gcd(k,q-1)>1$, and $n\equiv0\pmod{2k}$.

**Function-field Sárközy tightness conjecture.** Any such set satisfies

$$
|A|\leq q^{n\left(1-\frac{1}{k^2}\right)}.
$$

In particular, when $k=2$ and $q$ is odd, Theorem should be tight.

This conjecture predicts that the lower bound in the function-field Sárközy theorem is exact in the quadratic case. The source contrasts this with the gap between the known upper and lower bounds and notes related speculation in the integer setting.
record.source_name: Eric Naslund, “Paley Graphs and Sárközy's Theorem In Function Fields”, arXiv:2203.01293 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: The spanning 2-tree conjecture for maximal planar graphs
record.statement: Let a maximal planar graph be a planar graph to which no edge can be added while preserving planarity, and let a **spanning 2-tree** be a spanning subgraph that is a 2-tree. **Spanning 2-tree conjecture.** Every maximal planar graph with order $n\geq3$ contains a spanning 2-tree. This reframes Cai's question about whether every plane triangulation contains a spanning 2-tree; the problem is nontrivial because, unlike spanning trees and spanning 3-trees in planar graphs, the existence of a spanning 2-tree is not automatic. Special cases include 4-connected maximal planar graphs and 3-trees, but the general question remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Allan Bickle, “Plane Triangulations Without Spanning 2-Trees”, arXiv:2203.10239 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.10239

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: Arc-disjoint hamiltonian paths in Cartesian products of directed cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_1,C_2,\ldots,C_r$ be directed cycles of length at least $2$, and let $r\geq 2$. Their Cartesian product is the digraph

$$
C_1\mathbin{\Box}C_2\mathbin{\Box}\cdots\mathbin{\Box}C_r.
$$

**Arc-disjoint hamiltonian paths conjecture.** The Cartesian product $C_1\mathbin{\Box}C_2\mathbin{\Box}\cdots\mathbin{\Box}C_r$ has two arc-disjoint hamiltonian paths.

The claim is proved for $r=2$ and for $r\geq 4$ in the paper, leaving the case of Cartesian products of three directed cycles as the only open case. Several broad families of three-cycle products are also known to satisfy the claim.
record.source_name: Iren Darijani, Babak Miraftab and Dave Witte Morris, “Arc-disjoint hamiltonian paths in Cartesian products of directed cycles”, arXiv:2203.11017 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11017

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: Kalkowski–Karoński–Pfender's twin-free hypergraph conjecture
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 3$. Define

$$
\mathfrak{B}^{r}=\{\mathcal{H}:\mathcal{H}\text{ is an }r\text{-uniform hypergraph and }\chi^{e}(\mathcal{H})>2\}.
$$

Two vertices are twins when the sets of edges containing them are equal, and a hypergraph is twin-free when it contains no twins. **Kalkowski–Karoński–Pfender's twin-free hypergraph conjecture.** There is no twin-free hypergraph in $\mathfrak{B}^{r}$.
The conjecture says that every twin-free $r$-uniform hypergraph admits a neighbor sum distinguishing edge weighting using weights 1 and 2. The source gives examples in $\mathfrak{B}^{r}$ that have twins, but does not resolve whether a twin-free example exists.
record.source_name: Akbar Davoodi and Leila Maherani, “On the total versions of 1-2-3-conjecture for graphs and hypergraphs”, arXiv:2204.13936 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13936

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Matching conjecture for the Stanley inequality graph
record.statement: Let $\mathcal G=(V\sqcup W,E)$ be the bipartite graph defined above, with the parts and edges constructed from the relevant sets of linear extensions. **Matching conjecture.** There exists a maximal matching in $\mathcal G$ that covers every vertex in $W$. This conjecture proposes a matching-based route to a direct injection proving Stanley's inequality. The source notes that every vertex of $W$ has at least one incident edge, but does not establish the existence of a matching covering all of $W$.
record.source_name: Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak and Greta Panova, “Effective poset inequalities”, arXiv:2205.02798 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.02798

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: The improved degree bound for spanning closed trails in edge-connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-edge-connected graph, meaning every edge cut of $G$ has size at least $k$, with $k\geq 4$. A spanning closed trail is a closed trail containing every vertex of $G$. **The improved spanning-trail conjecture.** The graph $G$ admits a spanning closed trail meeting each vertex $v$ at most

$$
\left\lceil\frac{d_G(v)-2}{k}\right\rceil+1
$$

times. The source says that the preceding theorem can likely be improved to this simpler bound; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Morteza Hasanvand, “Spanning tree-connected subgraphs with small degrees”, arXiv:2205.05044 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05044

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: The path-energy conjecture for graphs with 2-connected components
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a graph that can be decomposed into $k$ 2-connected components, and let its path matrix be the matrix whose eigenvalues are called path eigenvalues. A **2-connected component** is a maximal subgraph that is 2-connected.

**The path-energy conjecture.** If the graph $M$ can be decomposed into $k$ 2-connected components, then its path matrix has exactly $k$ positive eigenvalues.

This generalizes the preceding claim from one 2-connected component to a decomposition into several such components. The supplied text gives no resolution or additional evidence, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Amol P. Narke, Prashant P. Malavadkar and Maruti M. Shikare, “Bounds on Path Energy of Graphs”, arXiv:2205.05100 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05100

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Infinite-family conjecture for 4-edge-critical pseudocircle arrangement graphs
record.statement:
A **simple arrangement** is an arrangement of pseudocircles with no three curves meeting at one point, and an arrangement graph is **4-edge-critical** when it is 4-chromatic and deleting any edge decreases its chromatic number.

**Infinite-family conjecture.** There exists an infinite family of simple arrangement graphs of 4-edge-critical arrangements of pseudocircles.

The paper constructs several examples and discusses infinite families of related critical planar graphs, but the asserted infinite family of simple pseudocircle arrangement graphs remains open.
record.source_name: Man-Kwun Chiu, Stefan Felsner, Manfred Scheucher, Felix Schröder, Raphael Steiner and Birgit Vogtenhuber, “Coloring circle arrangements: New 4-chromatic planar graphs”, arXiv:2205.08181 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08181

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Le's polynomial bound on induced paths in $\mathcal{O}_2$-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let an **$\mathcal{O}_2$-free graph** be a graph containing no induced subgraph from the family $\mathcal{O}_2$. An **induced path** is a path whose vertices induce exactly the edges of the path.

**Le's induced-path conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ such that every $\mathcal{O}_2$-free $n$-vertex graph has at most $n^c$ distinct induced paths.

This conjecture was raised earlier as an open question by Raymond. The paper places it in the context of recognizing $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs and does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Édouard Bonnet, Hugues Déprés, Louis Esperet, Colin Geniet, Claire Hilaire, Stéphan Thomassé and Alexandra Wesolek, “Sparse graphs with bounded induced cycle packing number have logarithmic treewidth”, arXiv:2206.00594 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00594

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2022). “For $k=2$, when no complete bipartite is excluded as a subgraph, Le conjectured the following, which had been raised as an open question earlier by Raymond .”

record.title: A strengthening of the thrackle conjecture for topological trees
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let there be $m$ topological trees such that every pair of trees intersects exactly once and every leaf of every tree belongs to $\mathcal{P}$. **Strengthened thrackle conjecture.** We conjecture that

$$
m\le n.
$$

This is posed as a strengthening of the thrackle conjecture, asserting a linear upper bound on the number of pairwise once-intersecting topological trees whose leaves lie in a prescribed set of points. The source does not indicate that this strengthening has been resolved.
record.source_name: Péter Ágoston, Gábor Damásdi, Balázs Keszegh and Dömötör Pálvölgyi, “Orientation of good covers”, arXiv:2206.01723 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.01723

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: Rainbow basis covering conjecture for 2-bounded partitions
record.statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-base matroid, and let $\mathcal{P}$ be a 2-bounded partition of $E(M)$, meaning that every partition class has size at most $2$. **Rainbow basis covering conjecture.** There is an integer $k$ such that $M$ can be covered by $k$ bases, one of which is rainbow with respect to $\mathcal{P}$. This is described as a weaker possible first step toward the two rainbow factorization conjectures and is left open.
record.source_name: Florian Hörsch, Tomáš Kaiser and Matthias Kriesell, “Rainbow bases in matroids”, arXiv:2206.10322 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.10322

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2022). “This conjecture was refuted by Kir\'aly by pointing to a result of Fekete and Szab\'o .”

record.title: Line-middle graph inequality conjecture for outer-connected domination
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n\ge 2$, and let $L(G)$ and $M(G)$ denote its line graph and middle graph, respectively. The **line-middle graph inequality conjecture** asserts that

$$
\gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(L(G)) \le \gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(M(G)).
$$

The inequality is supported by the preceding results, including strict inequality for wheels of order at least five; equality occurs for at least one connected graph of order four. A classification of graphs for which equality holds is posed separately as an open problem, while the general inequality remains open.
record.source_name: Farshad Kazemnejad, Behnaz Pahlavsay, Elisa Palezzato and Michele Torielli, “Connected and outer-connected domination number of middle graphs”, arXiv:2206.15439 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15439

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: The common blow-up conjecture for K4-free graphs
record.statement: A **blow-up** of a graph $F$ is obtained by replacing each vertex of $F$ by a non-empty independent set, possibly of a different size, and joining two such sets exactly when their corresponding vertices are adjacent in $F$. **Common blow-up conjecture.** If $F$ is non-empty and $K_4$-free, then there exists a blow-up of $F$ which is common. The conjecture is presented as a natural approach toward the broader $K_4$-barrier conjecture; the supplied text gives evidence for the broader claim but no resolution of this blow-up version.
record.source_name: Natalie Behague, Natasha Morrison and Jonathan A. Noel, “Common Pairs of Graphs”, arXiv:2208.02045 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02045

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2022). “Despite a great deal of recent progress , Sidorenko's Conjecture remains open.”

record.title: The odd-hole-length chromatic bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\ell\geq2$ be an integer and let $G$ be a finite simple undirected graph with girth

$$
g(G)=2\ell+1.
$$

Let $k$ be the number of distinct lengths occurring among the odd holes of $G$. **Odd-hole-length chromatic bound conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $(k+2)$-colorable.

For $k=1$, this predicts the preceding 3-colorability statement in the triangle-free equal-odd-hole-length setting. The source gives no resolution of this general quantitative conjecture.
record.source_name: Rong Chen, “Graphs with girth 2+1 and without longer odd holes are 3-colorable”, arXiv:2301.00112 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.00112

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: Shi and Shan's conjecture for tough connected $(P_2\cup kP_1)$-free graphs
record.statement: Let $k$ be an integer with $k\ge 4$, and let $G$ be a graph. Here $P_n$ denotes the path on $n$ vertices, $P_2\cup kP_1$ is the disjoint union of a two-vertex path and $k$ isolated vertices, a graph is **$1$-tough** when its toughness is at least $1$, and **$2k$-connected** when deleting fewer than $2k$ vertices leaves it connected. The graph is $(P_2\cup kP_1)$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $P_2\cup kP_1$. **Shi and Shan's conjecture.** Every $1$-tough, $2k$-connected $(P_2\cup kP_1)$-free graph is Hamiltonian. Shi and Shan had proved the analogous statement with $4$-toughness for $k\ge4$; the conjecture weakens the toughness requirement to $1$ and remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Leyou Xu, Chengli Li and Bo Zhou, “Hamiltonicity of 1-tough (P_2kP_1)-free graphs”, arXiv:2303.09741 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2210.10408](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.10408).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09741

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2023). “A complete graph is said to be $t$-tough for any $t>0$. Chv\'{a}tal's toughness conjecture, stating that there exists a constant $t_0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph with at least three vertices is Hamiltonian, is still open in general.”

record.title: Brewster–McGuinness–Moore–Noel conjecture on cycles in non-fcolorable graphs
record.statement:
Let $k\ge 3$ and let $G$ be a graph, with chromatic number denoted by $\chi(G)$. A cycle has length $0\bmod k$ when its length is divisible by $k$. **BrewsterfMcGuinnessfMoorefNoel conjecture.** If

$$
\chi(G)>k,
$$

then $G$ contains at least as many cycles of length $0\bmod k$ as the complete graph $K_{k+1}$; equivalently, it contains at least

$$
\frac{(k+1)(k-1)!}{2}
$$

cycles of length $0\bmod k$. This conjecture generalizes the known lower bound $(k-1)!/2$ for non-$k$-colorable graphs. The paper proves the conjecture for $k=3$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Sean Kim and Michael E. Picollelli, “4-Chromatic Graphs Have At Least 4 Cycles of Length 0 3”, arXiv:2312.05945 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.05945

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2023). “This conjecture was proven by Bollob\'as , with the bound subsequently improved by Thomassen .”

record.title: Two-component conjecture for friends-and-strangers graphs with a complete bipartite factor
record.statement: Let $Y$ be a connected bipartite graph on $n\ge 5$ vertices with no non-trivial cut edge and $Y\not=C_n$. The graph $\mathsf{FS}(K_{2,n-2},Y)$ is the friends-and-strangers graph associated with $K_{2,n-2}$ and $Y$. **Two-component conjecture.** The graph $\mathsf{FS}(K_{2,n-2},Y)$ has exactly $2$ components. Wilson's result establishes the analogous statement for $\mathsf{FS}(S_n,Y)$, and the cited theorem gives supporting evidence in the complete-bipartite case; the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Lanchao Wang, Junying Lu and Yaojun Chen, “Connectedness of friends-and-strangers graphs of complete bipartite graphs and others”, arXiv:2302.00900 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00900

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: The q-zero forcing conjecture for the Cartesian product of a complete bipartite graph and K_2
record.statement:
Let $K_{n,m}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $n$ and $m$, and let $K_2$ be the complete graph on two vertices. Write $Z_q(G)$ for the $q$-analogue of the zero forcing number of a graph $G$. **The q-zero forcing conjecture.** For any $n,m\geq 2$,

$$
Z_q(K_{n,m} \: \Box \: K_2)=
\begin{cases}
2\min(n,m) & \text{if } q=0,\\
n+m & \text{for } q\geq 1.
\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture proposes exact values of the $q$-zero forcing number for this Cartesian-product family; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Shaun Fallat, Neha Joshi, Roghayeh Maleki, Karen Meagher, Seyed Ahmad Mojallal, Shahla Nasserasr, Mahsa N. Shirazi, Andriaherimanana Sarobidy Razafimahatratra and Brett Stevens, “The q-Analogue of Zero Forcing for Certain Families of Graphs”, arXiv:2306.01138 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.01138

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).
